metadata.notes: 2026-08-21 PRESEASON UPDATE — FIRST SUBSTANTIVE CHANGE SINCE 2026-06-16. Football Zebras published the full 2026 crew-by-crew rosters on 2026-08-01, resolving the item this tracker had been waiting on since April. WHAT CHANGED: (1) All 17 crews now have confirmed 2026 on-field and replay personnel, attached per-crew under crew2026. (2) Swing officials identified: Greg Meyer (BJ, 25 yrs) and Tab Slaughter (U, 7 yrs). (3) A crew-continuity score was computed for every crew — how many of the 6 non-referee on-field positions returned — which determines how much 2025 tendency data should be trusted in 2026. Two crews are fully intact (Rogers, Moore); three have half or more of the crew replaced (Clark, Hussey, Vinovich). (4) Zero crew-chief changes; all 17 white hats return. (5) Seven rookie officials placed: Ray (Clark/LJ), Dimpfel (Eck/FJ), Fucik (Hill/SJ), Larrew (Hochuli/SJ), DeLeon (Hussey/FJ), Braun (Wrolstad/DJ), plus rehire Parham (Smith/SJ). (6) 2026 rule changes logged with penalty-impact assessments. (7) Nine officials taking referee reps; crew-of-6 drills in preseason. Tendency metrics themselves are unchanged 2025 aggregates and remain the best available baseline. NEXT SUBSTANTIVE UPDATE: Week 1 regular-season crew assignments, expected Tuesday 2026-09-08 (opener estimated 2026-09-10), when weekly polling resumes.

swingOfficials2026.matchupImpactNote: Swing officials rotate between crews week to week. Any game where Meyer (BJ) or Slaughter (U) substitutes carries elevated variance against that crew's baseline tendencies — Meyer at back judge affects deep-pass and DPI calls; Slaughter at umpire affects offensive holding, the single highest-volume penalty category. Weekly assignment data should flag substitutions, which Football Zebras notes occur regularly.

offseasonNotes.cbaStatus: RESOLVED AND IN EFFECT. The new 7-year CBA (ratified 2026-05-08 by a 116-4 NFLRA vote) took effect 2026-06-01, succeeding the prior agreement with no gap. There is no lockout and no replacement officials for 2026. The April-2026 stalemate narrative — owners including Jerry Jones at the table, sides 'far apart' on compensation, league 'preparing for a lockout,' replacement-official training scheduled for 2026-05-01 — is fully superseded and retained only as historical context in the cba2026 block below.
cbaStickingPoints: Salary: NFL offers 6.45–6.7% annual growth; NFLRA demands 10–10.3% + $2.5M marketing fees (league calls the marketing fees 'worthless')
Probationary period: NFL wants 5 years (up from 3); NFLRA opposes
Postseason assignments: NFL wants performance-based over seniority-based
Performance standards: NFLRA has been resistant to engage on performance-improvement mechanisms during talks, per league sources
Centralized officiating: NFL approved command-center monitoring in event of lockout

replacementOfficials.status: MOOT — CBA ratified 2026-05-08. Replacement-official program is being wound down. Replacement officials will NOT work any 2026 games. Training that began 2026-05-01 lasted ~one week before the deal was finalized.
replacementOfficials.compensationNote: Replacement officials hired during the lockout-prep period are being paid out per terms of their conditional contracts; the league has not publicly disclosed final figures.
replacementOfficials.nflpaPosition: Resolved — NFLPA supported NFLRA throughout; no further public friction.
replacementOfficials.historicalComparison: First serious replacement-ref threat since 2012; resolved without games being affected.
replacementOfficials.leagueOfficeBackstop: The 2026-only safeguard rule allowing the NY Officiating Department to call penalties remotely was tied to replacement-official use and is now functionally dormant — though the rule itself remains on the books for 2026 as adopted at the Annual League Meeting.

cba2026.summary: NFL and NFLRA reached a 7-year deal averting a lockout, ratified by a 116-4 NFLRA vote on 2026-05-08 and effective 2026-06-01. Sides negotiated for 2+ years and were publicly far apart (NFL 6.45–6.7% vs NFLRA 10–10.3% + $2.5M marketing fees) as recently as late April before recruiting of college replacement officials began in early March.
leagueGains: Increased access to officials in the offseason for a formal training program
Development of a 'bench' of officials (the swing-official model is now structural, not just a 2026 patch)
Greater latitude to use performance metrics for postseason assignments rather than seniority (previously a major NFLRA red line)
nflraGains: Compensation increases (specific percentages not publicly disclosed; final number is between the two opening positions)
Avoided performance-based probationary periods that the NFL had pushed for
cba2026.implicationsForTendencyProfiles: All 17 historical crew-chief profiles remain valid for 2026. The new performance-metric postseason-assignment rule could shift WHICH crews work playoff games in January 2027, but does NOT change in-season regular-game assignments or in-game tendencies.

ruleChanges2026: FORMALLY ADOPTED at Annual League Meeting (March 2026): five rule changes total — focused on kickoff adjustments and officiating-aid mechanisms.

FORMALLY ADOPTED: Replay can now consult with on-field officials on disqualifications for both flagrant football acts AND non-football acts — and can drop a flag when one is not thrown. Cited precedent: DK Metcalf vs. Detroit heckling-fan incident in 2025, where on-field officials did not see the swipe and replay could not act.

FORMALLY ADOPTED (1-year only, 2026 season): NFL Officiating Department empowered to correct 'clear and obvious' on-field misses that significantly affect the game in the event of a work stoppage involving NFLRA officials. Replay center in NY can call penalties remotely — a power the league has historically declined to use.
Centralized officiating command center for potential replacement-ref games (operational backstop to the rule change above).

personnelChanges2026.swingOfficialsNote: 7 hires filling 5 vacancies = 2 swing officials who rotate between crews throughout 2026 rather than being assigned to a single crew. New CBA formalizes this 'bench' model going forward.
personnelChanges2026.summary: Zero crew chief (referee / white hat) changes for 2026. All 17 white hats from 2025 return. All historical crew-chief tendency profiles remain VALID for 2026. Personnel turnover is entirely at the deep-official positions (FJ, SJ, DJ, LJ) where individual flag tendencies are absorbed into crew-level averages.

offseasonNotes.crewCompositionRisk: LOW — CBA ratified 2026-05-08. All 17 crew chiefs return. Deep-official turnover (4 retirements, 1 relegation, 7 new hires) is normal year-over-year churn and within historical bounds for crew-level tendency stability.
offseasonNotes.firstFullMeeting: May 2026 — first scheduled meeting of all NFL officials (including 7 new hires) — proceeding as planned now that CBA is ratified.

crews2026Confirmed.note: Full 2026 crew-by-crew rosters are now public — this is the substantive update the offseason tracker had been waiting on since April. 121 officials across 17 crews plus 2 swing officials. All 17 crew chiefs (white hats) from 2025 return. Roster math validates: 17 referees + 102 non-referee on-field positions + 2 swing = 121.

backupRefereeProgram2026.note: Nine officials are taking referee reps in 2026 for an undisclosed number of snaps. The league is also running crew-of-6 drills in preseason. Football Zebras confirms backup referees are working live preseason games (Larry Smith on the Hochuli crew, Bryan Neale on the Smith crew in preseason week 2). Watch for in-game referee swaps in the regular season, which would break the assumption that one white hat governs a full game's tendencies.

ruleChanges2026.source: NFL Annual League Meeting, approved April 2026

changes.detail: Touchback from a 50-yard-line kickoff now spots at the receiving team's 20 rather than 25. Minimum receiving-team players with front foot on the setup line drops 6 -> 5; maximum off the line rises 3 -> 4.
changes.modelNote: More kickoff variety means more setup-zone and formation infractions. Expect a modest uptick in kickoff-formation and illegal-touch flags early in the season while crews calibrate.

changes.change: League personnel may consult on-field officials on disqualifications
changes.detail: Officiating department can advise on flagrant football and non-football acts without being called onto the field.
changes.modelNote: Slightly raises the ceiling on ejections for personal fouls; does not change flag volume.

changes.change: League office authority to correct clear-and-obvious misses (2026 only)
changes.detail: Conditional on a work stoppage involving NFLRA-represented officials.
changes.modelNote: MOOT. The 7-year CBA ratified 2026-05-08 took effect 2026-06-01. No work stoppage, no replacement officials. This provision should not be modeled.

dataQualityFlags2026.detail: Football Zebras' 2026 crew article states 7 officials 'retired or were otherwise not retained' after 2025. This tracker has 4 confirmed retirements (Patterson, Cheek, Brown, Stephan) plus 1 relegation (Lo van Pham) = 5. Roughly 2 non-retentions were never individually announced. Immaterial to crew-level tendency modeling; the 2026 rosters are confirmed complete.

All tendency metrics in this file are 2025 regular-season crew-level aggregates. Crew composition changed for 15 of 17 crews. Use the per-crew crew2026.continuity.tendencyCarryoverConfidence field to weight how much of the 2025 signal should be trusted in 2026.

repo/src/data/intelligence/referee_profiles.json (which RefereeProfileCard.jsx imports) was last updated 2026-03-17 and contains Week-3-pace estimates rather than full-season 2025 stats. The canonical file at data/intelligence/referees/referee_profiles.json is five months ahead. Synced by this run.

Two known mismatches after syncing the fresh data into the repo. (1) volColor() and the compact 'Flag-Happy Crews' filter only recognize flagVolume values 'high' | 'moderate-high' | 'moderate' | 'low'. The current data also uses 'very high', 'very low', and 'low-moderate'. Consequence: Alex Moore — the league's flag-heaviest crew at 16.13/gm — is filtered OUT of the Flag-Happy Crews card because his value is 'very high', not 'high'. One-line fix: include 'very high' in the filter and add it to volOrder/volColor. (2) The detail panel reads tendencies.estimatedPenaltiesPerGame and tendencies.penaltyYardsWeek3, which were Week-3-pace fields from the March data and no longer exist. Point them at season2025Stats.penaltiesPerGame and season2025Stats.yardsPerGame instead — those two stat tiles currently render empty. (3) Optional upside: crew2026.continuity is now available per crew and is the most decision-relevant new field in the dataset — worth surfacing as a confidence badge on each crew.
